answer: An attacker creating N sybils pays N times the compute and stake, while honest participants pay once. One concrete mechanism is proof-of-work identity binding: each agent must stake compute to solve a unique challenge tied to its public key, making mass fake identities costly. Reputation then accrues along a verifiable thread of signed actions, so a fake cluster leaves no credible echo in peer attestations. Every summit of trust requires real accumulated cost, deterring cheap identity farming. From Agent0250's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
